candidate.title: Frag-seq
candidate.scope: Assigned Illumina Frag-seq row: an in vitro RNA structure-probing architecture with separate P1, endogenous 5′P, and kinase-treated endogenous 5′OH control routes through end-dependent fragment capture, reverse transcription and cDNA. FragSeq/fragmentation sequencing is the primary paper’s name for this target. The diagram’s “in vitro folded polyA RNA” preparation history is preserved; its difference from the original nuclear-RNA implementation is explicitly corrected below. PARTE above and CapSeq below are neighboring poster rows, not alternative targets of this assigned schematic. Sequencing, scoring and routine library details beyond the drawn cDNA endpoint are discussed only to interpret the readout.

states.label: RNA input for in vitro structure probing
features: Drawing labels this material “In vitro folded polyA RNA” and represents a stem-loop; the leftmost “Fragmentation sequencing (Frag-seq)” icon illustrates the assay target rather than a separate preparation step.

Primary-source resolution: the identified original FragSeq implementation probed naked mouse nuclear RNA, including ncRNAs. Its biological target is RNA accessibility/structure; polyA selection is not established for that implementation by the supplied paper.
All three routes below retain the drawing’s stated folded-polyA preparation history at schematic scope; the primary-source clarification does not silently replace this input.

operations.label: P1 endonuclease digestion
operations.description: P1 cleaves the RNA backbone in accessible single-stranded regions, turning folded RNA into fragments with new cleavage ends. The green P1 icon is a catalyst, not an RNA product.
operations.mechanism: P1 preferentially cleaves single-stranded nucleic acid and produces 5′ monophosphate / 3′OH termini under the primary implementation’s tested conditions.
operations.information_effect: Fragment-end positions provide a physical record of susceptibility to P1. This is a structure-dependent accessibility readout, not uniform transcript coverage. A missing cut is not proof of base pairing: the primary study reports missed small interior loops/bulges and fragments excluded by the cloning size window.
